mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in CPIAUCSL above 203.5 signals accelerating inflation, which triggers equity market risk aversion and produces negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as real rates rise.
failure_condition: SPX 20d returns remain positive in >60% of instances where CPIAUCSL > 203.5, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in UNRATE below 4.5% signals labor market tightening, increasing wage-push inflation risks and causing negative S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days as monetary policy responds.
failure_condition: SPX 5d returns are positive in >50% of triggered instances, or UNRATE < 4.5 correlates with positive returns in 2006-2024 data.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in HOUST and GDPC1 below 1650 and 11300 respectively signal weakening consumer demand, triggering negative S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days as recession risks materialize.
failure_condition: Either HOUST < 1650 or GDPC1 < 11300 alone predicts negative returns, or joint signal fails to correlate with negative SPX 60d returns.

mechanism_narrative: A 10% monthly decline in INDPRO below 100 signals industrial production slowdown, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days as recession fears dominate equity pricing.
failure_condition: INDPRO < 100 correlates with positive SPX 20d returns in >40% of cases, or Rank IC < 0.02 over 2006-2024.

mechanism_narrative: FEDFUNDS exceeding 5.25% signals active monetary tightening, compressing equity valuations through higher discount rates and producing negative S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5d returns are positive in >55% of FEDFUNDS > 5.25 instances, or signal fails to outperform baseline returns.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in RSAFS above 350,000 signals rising consumer spending, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days as earnings growth expectations rise.
failure_condition: RSAFS > 350,000 correlates with negative SPX 20d returns in >45% of cases, or Rank IC < 0.03 over 2006-2024.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous PAYEMS growth above 135,000 and UNRATE decline below 4.5% signal labor market strength, producing positive S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days as wage growth supports consumption.
failure_condition: Either PAYEMS > 135000 or UNRATE < 4.5 alone predicts positive returns, or joint signal fails to correlate with positive SPX 60d returns.

mechanism_narrative: A 15% monthly drop in INDPRO below 100 during late-cycle expansion triggers negative S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days as manufacturing slowdowns signal economic deceleration.
failure_condition: INDPRO < 100 correlates with positive SPX 60d returns in >50% of late-cycle instances, or signal fails to distinguish from baseline returns.
